scenario: AITA for having a photo of me with my friend’s girlfriend as my phone wallpaper? | I’m 23M. My friend Charley and I were tight back in college. We even lived together our second year. We’re still friends, but we kind of diverged. He found early success in his career and dating life, while I’m still single and doing entry level work. He started dating this model since last summer. I met her at a New Year’s party when Charley brought her. I knew about her since before Charley even started dating her. I follow a lot of models on Instagram and Charley’s girlfriend was one of them, but I wouldn’t call her a celebrity among the general public, especially in a city full of stars like LA. But anyways, I found her to be extremely pretty and introduced myself as a fan and asked her for a photo together. Charley took it. I respected their relationship and didn’t post that photo on social media, but rather used it as my phone wallpaper. She’s eye candy and it motivates me to work hard like Charley so hopefully one day I can call someone like her my girlfriend. She’s really sweet. Charley’s really lucky. I try my best to not be a creep around her or when discussing her with Charley. Yesterday, I had dinner with just Charley. We had a good time catching up. We didn’t talk much about his girlfriend until he noticed my phone wallpaper as we were waiting for the check. I wrote down a reminder to change that before meeting up with Charley yesterday, but I forgot about it. He asked me why I had that photo as my wallpaper. I was a little embarrassed and hesitated to speak for a few seconds. I just told Charley what I have already told him before, that I was a fan of her before they even started dating, but I respect their relationship and he doesn’t have anything to worry about. Charley never ridiculed me for not being good with women, but yesterday he told me that of course he doesn’t have to worry about me because a guy like me would never get a girl like her. I was really hurt by his words. I told Charley that he might be tall, good-looking, and make a lot of money, but he’s a huge dickhead for saying that. He said he’d rather be the world’s biggest dickhead than be me. I was speechless. He started playing on his phone. Our bill arrived and it came to $63. I put down $40 and walked out. I still haven’t gotten an apology from Charley.

It’s not just about admiration; it’s about **owning a visual representation of someone else’s partner** in a way that’s inherently possessive or invasive. Even if you didn’t post it publicly, the act itself signals disrespect for her boundaries (and Charley’s relationship). - **The "Fan" Excuse Doesn’t Hold Up**: You followed her on Instagram *before* she was Charley’s girlfriend, but that doesn’t change the fact that she’s now in a committed relationship. Using her image as wallpaper—especially after meeting her in person—implies you’re **claiming her as yours in some way**, which is unfair to both her and Charley. ### **The Worse Part: Charley’s Reaction** - His comment (*"a guy like you would never get a girl like her"*) was **rude and unnecessary**, but it’s also a **reaction to your behavior**. He likely felt uncomfortable because your wallpaper sent the wrong message—like you were **competing for her attention** or treating her as a trophy. His response was harsh, but it was a **natural reaction to what you did**. - Your reaction (*"he’s a huge dickhead"*) was justified, but your **walking out without paying the full bill** was petty and childish. It escalated the conflict unnecessarily. ### **Why This Is Still Wrong (Even If You Meant Well)** 1. **You Put Her in an Uncomfortable Position**: Even if she’s a public figure (a model), she’s still a person in a relationship. Using her image as wallpaper—especially after meeting her—puts her in the awkward position of knowing someone is **displaying her as their personal inspiration**. 2. **It’s a Form of Objectification**: You’re treating her like a **motivational poster**, not a real person with her own life. That’s disrespectful, even if you claim it’s "just for inspiration." 3. **You Didn’t Respect Charley’s Relationship**: Even if you didn’t post it publicly, the fact that you **chose her image to represent yourself** (on your phone, which he saw) implies you’re **prioritizing her over his relationship**. That’s not how you treat a friend’s partner. ### **What You Should Have Done** - **Deleted the wallpaper immediately** after realizing Charley saw it. - **Apologized sincerely** to Charley for making him uncomfortable, even if you didn’t mean to. - **Avoided using her as a "motivational tool"**—if you want to work hard for a partner like her, **act like someone who deserves her**, not someone who **displays her as a status symbol**. ### **Final Verdict: 0 (Not Acceptable)** While your intentions might have been harmless (or even flattering), the **action itself was disrespectful**. Charley’s reaction was over-the-top, but it was a **natural response to what you did**. The fact that you **walked out without paying** only made things worse. **Lesson:** If you admire someone, admire them **without making them feel like your personal property**. If you want a partner like her, **be the kind of person who earns that relationship—not the kind who treats it like a trophy.**
